summary: Modern databases have evolved far beyond storage and retrieval, embedding AI/ML capabilities directly into the data layer to eliminate costly data movement and simplify production AI pipelines. By 2026, vector search has become a standard feature across nearly every major database platform, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities. Leading platforms like Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML, and Databricks now offer native LLM inference, embedding generation, and MLOps tooling directly alongside transactional and analytical workloads.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides fully managed LLM inference, embedding generation, text classification, summarization, and sentiment analysis directly within the Snowflake AI Data Cloud using SQL functions. Snowflake Postgres now runs natively in the AI Data Cloud with pgvector support and Cortex integration, making it possible to run vector similarity search and LLM-powered queries on governed enterprise data without moving it outside Snowflake. Cortex also includes Cortex Search for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines and Cortex Analyst for natural language querying of structured data.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM inference via Cortex functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, TRANSLATE, EMBED_TEXT) supporting models including Mistral, LLaMA, Reka, and Arctic. Cortex Search enables RAG workflows. Snowflake Postgres with pgvector adds vector similarity search natively integrated with Cortex AI functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed in Snowflake credits per token processed. Embedding and inference costs vary by model selected. Snowflake Postgres pricing is usage-based and generally available as of early 2026. Overall cost is tied to compute credits consumed, with no separate per-query LLM API cost for supported hosted models.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML and Vertex AI Integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data analysts and engineers to build, train, and deploy ML models directly in BigQuery using standard SQL, supporting regression, classification, clustering, time-series forecasting, and deep learning models. BigQuery integrates natively with Google Vertex AI, enabling remote model inference against deployed Vertex endpoints and foundation models such as Gemini directly from BigQuery SQL. BigQuery Vector Search enables approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns stored as ARRAY<FLOAT64>, supporting RAG pipelines and semantic search at petabyte scale without exporting data.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Google Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 1.5 Flash) and other Vertex AI foundation models via the ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT SQL functions. Supports embedding generation and LLM prompting entirely within BigQuery SQL, with results stored back as standard tables.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference billed per byte processed for SQL queries plus separate Vertex AI model inference costs per 1,000 characters or tokens depending on model. BigQuery Vector Search is included in standard BigQuery on-demand or flat-rate pricing. Vertex AI LLM calls add cost on top of BigQuery compute.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds a native vector data type and enables exact and approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW and IVFFlat indexing, making it the lowest-friction path to vector search for teams already running Postgres with no new infrastructure required. pgai is a complementary extension that brings LLM embedding generation and inference directly into Postgres SQL, allowing rows to be embedded or queried against LLMs without leaving the database. Together they support full RAG pipelines, semantic search, and AI-augmented queries entirely within a standard Postgres instance, integrating well with Snowflake and Databricks environments for hybrid architectures. pgvector handles up to 50 million vectors comfortably for most production RAG workloads.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension supports integration with OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic Claude, and Cohere APIs directly from SQL functions such as ai.openai_embed() and ai.openai_chat_complete(). Vectorizer feature in pgai automates embedding generation and synchronization for table columns. Works natively within Snowflake Postgres with Cortex AI functions as of 2026.
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to use. Costs are limited to the underlying Postgres infrastructure (self-hosted or managed via services like Supabase, Neon, AWS RDS, or Snowflake Postgres) plus any external LLM API call costs (e.g., OpenAI API pricing per token). Managed Postgres offerings with pgvector enabled typically add a small infrastructure premium.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML enables applications to call Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock foundation models directly from Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL using SQL functions, allowing inference on relational data without data movement. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports pgvector for vector similarity search, enabling RAG and semantic search workloads within the managed Aurora environment. Redshift ML allows data teams to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL by integrating with Amazon SageMaker AutoPilot, and supports calling Bedrock LLMs for text inference directly from Redshift SQL queries, making both OLTP and OLAP workloads AI-capable within the AWS ecosystem.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector for vector search and integrates with Amazon Bedrock (Claude, Titan, Llama, Mistral) and SageMaker endpoints via SQL functions. Redshift ML integrates with SageMaker AutoPilot for model training and Amazon Bedrock for LLM inference. Both services use IAM-based authorization to call AI services without managing credentials separately.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML inference calls are billed by SageMaker or Bedrock invocation costs in addition to standard Aurora instance pricing. Redshift ML model training incurs SageMaker AutoPilot costs; Bedrock inference calls are billed per token or per request per model. Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector has no additional license cost beyond standard Aurora pricing. Costs can grow significantly at high inference volumes.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI: MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, and Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks provides a comprehensive AI and ML platform centered on Mosaic AI, which unifies model training, fine-tuning, serving, and evaluation with MLflow as the open-source backbone for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment lifecycle management. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database built into the Lakehouse that indexes Delta Lake tables and keeps vector indexes automatically synchronized as underlying data changes, enabling production RAG pipelines without separate vector infrastructure. DBRX is Databricks' own open-source LLM available for fine-tuning and inference on the platform, and Databricks integrates with external models via AI Gateway, supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers with unified rate limiting and cost tracking. pgvector integrates well with Databricks environments for teams preferring Postgres-based vector storage alongside Databricks compute.
databases.llm_integration: Native support for DBRX, LLaMA, Mistral, and other open-source LLMs via Mosaic AI Model Serving with GPU-backed endpoints. AI Gateway provides a unified proxy to OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and other external LLM APIs with centralized governance. MLflow LLM evaluation tools support benchmarking and quality tracking for RAG and agent pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: MLflow is open-source and free. Databricks billing is DBU (Databricks Unit) based, covering compute for training, fine-tuning, and serving. Vector Search is included in Databricks Premium and Enterprise tiers with additional DBU consumption for index serving. Model serving costs vary by GPU instance type and throughput. DBRX inference on Databricks is billed by DBUs consumed per token at serving time.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search adds approximate nearest neighbor vector search natively to MongoDB Atlas collections using HNSW indexing, allowing applications to store embeddings alongside source documents in the same document model and query them with the standard MongoDB aggregation pipeline. This eliminates the need for a separate vector database by unifying operational data and vector search in one managed platform, supporting RAG architectures where context retrieval and data serving happen from a single store. Atlas Vector Search supports hybrid search combining vector similarity with full-text search using Atlas Search, and integrates with major AI frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Hugging Face for end-to-end AI application development.
databases.llm_integration: Atlas Vector Search integrates with OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock, Hugging Face, and Cohere for embedding generation and LLM inference via official LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations. MongoDB Atlas does not host LLMs natively but provides tight SDK integration with all major LLM providers. Atlas also offers a built-in Data API and App Services triggers to automate embedding updates on document writes.
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is available on M10 dedicated clusters and above with no additional charge for the vector search feature itself on paid tiers. Free tier (M0) does not support Vector Search. Costs scale with Atlas cluster size (compute and storage). Embedding generation and LLM inference costs are separate and determined by the external AI provider used.
